# ACP-family replay fixtures (#48)

The `acp`, `grok`, `cursor`, `kimi` and `fx` transcripts in this directory
replay Waku's ACP `DriverV2` (`src/driver/acp/`). Their assertions are in
`tests/replay_acp.rs`.

**No agent CLI was run to make them.** Every file is generated by
[`../replay-sources/acp_fixtures.py`](../replay-sources/acp_fixtures.py) from
T3 Code's recorded Grok ACP transcripts and from frames written to the ACP
spec. All of them carry `"synthetic": true` and a `source` in their header.

```
python3 -I crates/waku-core/fixtures/replay-sources/acp_fixtures.py \
  <t3code checkout> crates/waku-core/fixtures/replay
```

T3's transcripts live at
`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/fixtures/<scenario>/grok_transcript.ndjson`
(T3 recorded Grok 1.0.41). The live smoke test against the real CLIs (port
step 13) has not been run.

## How T3's frames were adapted

- T3 records logical frames without JSON-RPC ids (`{"kind":"request",…}`).
  The generator gives Waku's requests ids from 1 per process, as the driver
  does, and answers each response to the open request of its method. It gives
  agent→client requests ids from 0.
- Outbound frames are what Waku sends, not what T3 sent. This covers
  `initialize`, `session/new`, the prompt text (the scenario's own input, not
  T3's instructions envelope), and `session/cancel` (Waku sends no
  `_meta.cancelTrigger`). T3's `session/close` and everything after it are
  dropped: Waku shuts the agent down by closing stdin.
- T3's prompt ids `t3-xai-prompt-N` become `waku-prompt-N` in every inbound
  frame.
- Inbound frames are kept verbatim otherwise, including Grok's `_x.ai/*`
  notifications. The driver must ignore those, and the fixtures prove that it
  does.
- **The non-Grok flavors** (`acp`, `cursor`, `kimi`, `fx`) use the same frames
  with every `_x.ai/*` notification and every `_meta` removed. They also use a
  spec-only `initialize` result (ACP v1, `loadSession: true`, nothing
  unstable). Their launch lines are their own: `cursor-agent acp`, `kimi acp`,
  `fx acp`, and `acp-agent` for the generic agent. Cursor also gets its
  `parameterizedModelPicker` opt-in. None of these agents' real payloads were
  recorded.

## Sources per scenario

| Scenario | Flavors | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `simple` | all | T3 `simple` (Grok) |
| `multi_turn` | all | T3 `multi_turn` (Grok) |
| `tool_call_read_only` | all | T3 `tool_call_read_only` (Grok) |
| `tool_call_approval` | all | T3 `tool_call_read_only_on_request` (Grok's real `session/request_permission`, option ids `allow-edits-session` / `allow-once` / `reject-once`); run in Supervised mode via `input.<flavor>.json` |
| `plan_questions` | grok, cursor | Grok: T3 `plan_questions` (`_x.ai/ask_user_question`). Cursor: written from the `cursor/ask_question` shape Waku's v1 driver handled, plus ACP `plan` updates |
| `turn_interrupt` | all | written: the cancel half of T3 `message_steering` |
| `turn_interrupt_mid_tool` | all | written from the ACP spec (`execute` tool call, `session/cancel`) |
| `steering_restart` | all | T3 `message_steering` (Grok): cancel, `cancelled`, then a new prompt |
| `provider_thread_resume` | all | written: Grok `session/resume`; the others `session/load`, whose replayed history must not become live messages |
| `usage_limit` | all | Grok: T3 `grok_prompt_error` shape with the `rate_limit` stop reason and code `-32003` (T3's classification). Others: a JSON-RPC error with `http_status: 429` and `resetAt` |
| `runtime_exit_unexpected` | all | written: the agent crashes mid-turn (`runtime_exit` `error`) |
| `thread_rollback` | grok | written from the fork protocol Waku's `grok_session` used: `_x.ai/session/fork` on channel `fork-1`, then on-disk truncation of `grok.home/.grok/sessions/…` |
| `thread_fork_native` | grok | same as `thread_rollback` |

`tool_call_approval/input.<flavor>.json` and `plan_questions/input.<flavor>.json`
override the shared steps. The shared steps were written for the fake agent:
an approval needs Supervised mode and the agent's own option id, and a
question needs the agent's own question id.
